item.title: Ballet Shoes - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Text of the day: “Let them. You have a job to do. For the next six weeks, you are going to be a kind and conscientious understudy. Which isn’t such a terrible thing to be, because for the next six weeks, you’ll still be in a theatre. So use this time. Watch. Enjoy. Learn.” (Sylvia in Kendall Feaver’s Ballet Shoes) quotation

item.title: Guess How Much I Love You? - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Favourite stage direction: “He fiddles with his phone for a bit... And chooses ‘Pale Blue Eyes’ by The Velvet Underground.” (Luke Norris’s Guess How Much I Love You?) quotation

item.title: Maggots - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Favourite stage direction: “A moment. The Storytellers look to each other, then the audience.” (Farah Najib’s Maggots) Quotation

item.title: Lost Atoms - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Text of the day: “Lots of folk tales start with a foolish act. Jack sells his cow for beans. Red Riding Hood confides in the wolf. The brave and curious fool follows their impulse and begins the quest that will lead to them becoming hero.” (Jess in Anna Jordan’s Lost Atoms) quotation

item.title: The Shitheads - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Favourite stage direction: “All of the characters are early human beings. No attempt should be made to make the two different groups the characters belong to physically distinct, and it is not necessary they look historically accurate.” (Jack Nicholls’s The Shitheads) quotation

item.title: Donbas - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Text of the day: “When they caught me I thought, maybe this is it. But the Cossacks used to say, ‘a good dying is when you don’t run’. You meet it head on. They believed if you die like that, the land takes you in — you don’t vanish, you become part of it: soil, wind, river. When the horses gallop, you’re in the sound of their hooves. The Steppe remembers the good ones, they feed what comes next. That’s the good death.” (Sashko in Olga Braga’s Donbas) quotation

item.title: Arcadia - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Text of the day: “Newton’s equations go forwards and backwards, they do not care which way. But the heat equation cares very much, it goes only one way.” (Thomasina in Tom Stoppard’s Arcadia) quotation

item.title: Magda Romanska’s Digital Access to the Performing Arts - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Magda Romanska’s excellent new book gives a thorough international overview of the digital arts during and after the pandemic review by Aleks Sierz

item.title: Arcadia - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Favourite stage direction: “The action of the play shuttles back and forth between the early nineteenth century and the present day, always in this same room.” (Tom Stoppard’s Arcadia) quotation

item.title: The Holy Rosenbergs - Aleks Sierz
item.description: Text of the day: “The world’s getting more dangerous for us by the day. You think we’re safe here? In cosy England? It’s a myth. We’ve had to triple security at the synagogue in the last few years.” (Saul in Ryan Craig’s The Holy Rosenbergs) Quotation
